_meta.purpose: MicroPython target-board profiles for checking whether this app fits a device. Used by tools/check_device_fit.py.
important: flash_mb is the chip's total flash (headline spec). fs_free_kb is the APPROX user-filesystem space left after a stock MicroPython firmware is flashed - that is the number your app's uploaded files actually compete for. It varies by firmware version; treat it as a guide and confirm on-device with os.statvfs('/').

ram_kb is the chip's total SRAM. heap_free_kb is the APPROX MicroPython free heap after boot - always much smaller than ram_kb on ESP32/ESP8266 because the WiFi stack / IDF reserve most SRAM. RAM fit can only be confirmed on-device with gc.mem_free(); the numbers here are for rough sizing only.
This app needs WiFi + an asyncio HTTP/WebSocket server, so it is heavier than a blink demo. Boards with heap_free_kb under ~64 are risky.
_meta.schema: key -> {name, mcu, ram_kb, heap_free_kb, flash_mb, fs_free_kb, wifi, notes}

rpi-pico.name: Raspberry Pi Pico
rpi-pico.notes: No onboard WiFi - this app's networking will not work without an add-on module.

rpi-pico-w.name: Raspberry Pi Pico W
rpi-pico-w.notes: WiFi stack reduces free heap vs the non-W Pico.

rpi-pico2-w.name: Raspberry Pi Pico 2 W
rpi-pico2-w.notes: THIS PROJECT'S CURRENT TARGET (see Pipfile stubs). Roomy for this app.

esp32-generic.name: ESP32 (generic, 4MB)
esp32-generic.notes: 520KB SRAM but MicroPython free heap is only ~100-160KB after WiFi init. Doable but tighter than RP2350.

esp32-s3.name: ESP32-S3 (8MB, no PSRAM)
esp32-s3.notes: Variants with PSRAM expose multiple MB of heap; without PSRAM expect ~180-260KB.

esp8266.name: ESP8266 (generic)
esp8266.notes: ~35KB free heap. An asyncio web server + this app is very likely to run out of RAM. Not recommended.

pyboard-v1.1.name: PyBoard v1.1
pyboard-v1.1.notes: No WiFi; small internal FS (use an SD card for www/). Flash is tight for the web bundle.
